- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.3) or shows sharp reversal, model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes — especially if sentiment is neutral or mixed — leading to over-forecasted peaks; apply lagged smoothing or dampen momentum.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is significantly above recent 5-10 day average, reduce by 5-10% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum; if sentiment turns bullish mid-horizon, adjust forecast upward by 2-5% in final 7-10 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +1 → -1 → +1), model tends to mispredict direction; use sentiment-weighted moving average for direction correction.
